summary: You pick a subplan and its own rules apply. Atmosphere/Energy: eight letter-graded core courses (3+5, 4+4 or 5+3) inside 30 A/E units, plus 15 advisor-approved units you move in. Sustainable Design and Construction: your track's required courses and area units. Environmental: the engineering core, seminars, policy, one depth focus area of three courses plus one course in each of two others (18 units) and 13 breadth units, with 27 units in CEE. Structural and Mechanics & Computation: the core inside 30 letter-graded program units, with 36 School of Engineering units and 36 letter-graded units. Sustainable Engineered Systems: its course splits. For every subplan the audit counts 45 graduate units at Stanford, none below the 100 level, at least 30 at 200 or above and 24 in the School of Engineering. You check by hand the 3.0 GPA, the program proposal, and the caps on CR/NC, seminar, research and practical training units.
